body:
## Problem

I find I'm used to hitting `<CR>` to skip past messages and I'd like to have it dismiss the ui2 window, rather than focus it, keeping both `:messages` and `g<` to focus it

## Solution

Allow the `<CR>` for entering the ui2 window to be configurable

## Alternate solution

Allow "real" mappings to enter the ui2 window, instead of reading the last typed characters

comment_data.body:
This assumes `<CR>` is the fallback - alternative option is to do nothing:

```diff
-local cr = vim.keycode('<CR>')
 vim.keymap.set('n', '<Plug>(nvim-pager)', function()
-  return M.cmd_on_key and 'g<' or cr
+  return M.cmd_on_key and 'g<' or nil
```

and leave the user of the mapping to handle falling back to `<CR>`:

```vim
nnoremap <expr>
\ <CR>
\ pager_open() ? "\<Plug>(nvim-pager)" : "\<CR>"
```

comment_regular_data.body:
i think we should drop this default behavior, it's not reliable enough, sometimes i end up n the pager when i don't want to be.

anyway, we should try to avoid adding a random option for this, as this PR does. the pager/msgarea/etc already set `filetype` and you can set or unset mappings on `FileType` event. if that doesn't work, can we figure out why, and make it work?

cc @luukvbaal

Sounds good. I'll change this PR to:
- remove `<CR>` and `g<`
- make `g<` a [default mapping](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/fbcb7a056cef7a5efd7aa7f494365a04b1c86895/runtime/doc/vim_diff.txt#L142-L178)
  - Since the behaviour of it and `:messages` is slightly different (`g<` showing just the most recent slew of messages), perhaps mapping `g<` to something like `:messages recent` ?

Will wait to see what @luukvbaal says first though.

> * remove `<CR>` and `g<`

`g<` shouldn't be removed...

> perhaps mapping `g<` to something like `:messages recent` ?

we can claim `g>` for that.

Sorry I wasn't clear at all there. What I meant:

<details><summary>

`:messages` and `g<` behave differently at the moment, the former shows all messages, `g<` shows only the most recent batch of messages

</summary>

---

```vim
:echom 'first'
:echom 'second'
```
`g<` shows just "second", whereas `:messages` shows both

---

</details>

With that I mind, I suggest:

- `<CR>` is removed from the [hard-coded check](https://github.com/bobrippling/neovim/blob/4a5062cda69fa6cb59b7dc0c488dfb05accf99de/runtime/lua/vim/_core/ui2/messages.lua#L589)
  -  (as you [mentioned above](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/40993#issuecomment-5085534138) if I've understood)
- `g<` is changed from being hard-coded to a default-mapping
  - This allows users to set or unset mappings on `FileType` events
  - One problem: the default-mapping needs to trigger a shorter version of `:messages`. Since it's not hardcoded/privvy to the implementation, we need to expose this functionality somehow, perhaps a `:messages recent`/`:messages latest` ?

> `g<` is changed from being hard-coded to a default-mapping

there's no reason to do this

> > `g<` is changed from being hard-coded to a default-mapping
> 
> there's no reason to do this

Sure - I think I misunderstood whether you were talking about just `<CR>` or it and `g<`. Pushed the removal of `<CR>`.

As a note, looks like `FileType` is fired when quitting the pager, oddly. But for entering the pager I suppose it doesn't come into play

I'll sort out the test failure

> Allow the `<CR>` for entering the ui2 window to be configurable

is this still relevant after https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/41062 ?

> > Allow the `<CR>` for entering the ui2 window to be configurable
> 
> is this still relevant after #41062 ?

Ah yes, after seeing ui2 messages I tend to hit `<CR>` to move to the next line in my buffer, so I think the mapping still gets in the way, if you see

the title is outdated. but actually, to make this configurable perhaps we could define a `<Plug>(nvim-pager)` mapping. So instead of checking for hardcoded `CR`, check for that. hopefully the `on_key` callback can see the `<plug>...` value in one of its args. may need to use `vim.keycode()` to compare it.
Got it, sorted the `<Plug>` mapping - got a few tweaks to make still, will ping/un-draft when ready

## Status

This is a stop-gap for now. We still need to figure out how to make `pager_char` avoid annoying "false positives".

Maybe a `CmdAtom` event could be used instead of of `on_key`, for this mapping...
